thread.title: Pandora earnings: New CEO is spending, how will investors react?

author: Emily Bary
title: Pandora earnings: New CEO is spending, how will investors react?
text:
Pandora Media Inc. has said that it will take time and money for the company to catch up to its digital peers, and the fourth-quarter earnings report expected after the bell Wednesday will be the first major test of investors’ patience. 
The streaming-music pioneer has begun a number of efforts recently to get its business on track, including giving users of its ad-supported radio product the ability to briefly play songs on demand in exchange for watching a short ad, an option it calls Premium Access. The move is intended to reverse a decline in listener hours and better compete with services like Spotify and Apple Music. 
“That helps us address the No. 1 reason people were leaving Pandora P, +4.65% but it also enables us to now use marketing, which we do well for our advertisers but don’t use at all for our own advertising,” Pandora CEO Roger Lynch told MarketWatch at CES in January. 
The idea is that if Pandora knows that you’re a Blake Shelton fan, it can now notify you that he has a new single and allow you to play that song on demand, which previously wasn’t possible within the standard online-radio service. It will also enable the company to work with artists who want to target their fans through ads. 
Despite the addition of that long-awaited feature for ad-supported listeners at the end of the December quarter, analysts predict that Pandora’s revenue for the period fell slightly relative to a year earlier. Consensus estimates call for $375.8 million in revenue and a 7 cent loss per share, according to FactSet.
Pandora has posted adjusted losses in the past seven quarters, and it’s expected to do so again for the December period after management spoke of the need to invest heavily in ad technology to improve measurability and give advertisers a better return on their investments. 
“Like you would get from Google GOOGL, +1.65% GOOG, +1.54% or Facebook FB, -0.30% in display, we need to do that for audio,” said Lynch, who took over as CEO in September. 
What to expect: 
Earnings: Analysts tracked by FactSet predict that Pandora will report a 7 cent loss per share for the December quarter. It posted a 13 cent loss per share a year earlier. According to Estimize, which crowdsources estimates from analysts, fund managers and academics, the average projection calls for a 4 cent loss per share. 
Revenue: Analysts on average expect revenue to fall to $375.8 million for the December quarter from $392.6 million a year earlier, according to FactSet. Estimize projects revenue of $377 million.
Stock movement: Shares of Pandora have declined 61% over the past 12 months. They’ve fallen after six of the company’s last 10 earnings reports, including a 25% drop in November when the company posted its third-quarter numbers and management spoke of the investments it would need to make in the business. 

A total of 30 analysts cover Pandora, according to FactSet, with 10 rating the stock a buy, 19 rating it a hold, and one rating it a sell. The average price target among these analysts is $7.68, 44% above current levels.
What to watch for 
Listener hours is a key metric to pay attention for in Pandora’s earnings. SunTrust Robinson Humphrey analyst Matthew Thornton recently wrote that consensus estimates for 5.1 billion listener hours seemed like “a low hurdle” given his take on third-party data as well as the launch of Premium Access. He predicts 5.25 billion listener hours for the quarter. The metric includes time spent listening to the company’s free ad-supported service and its two tiers of paid products.
Though Pandora has been placing heavy emphasis on the ad-radio product, it will be worth paying attention to subscription numbers, especially if the company discloses them for Pandora Premium, a fully on-demand service that competes directly with Apple Inc.’s AAPL, +0.60% Apple Music as well as Spotify. Pandora said that Premium crossed 1 million subscribers in October, and efforts to introduce some on-demand listening into its two radio products could prompt more users to upgrade to Premium and get a fully on-demand experience. Overall paid subscribers—which includes those who use Pandora Plus, an ad-free radio service—hit 5.2 million as of the end of September.
Look also for any additional information about how voice-controlled devices are contributing to results and listener hours. Lynch said that time spent listening to Pandora on voice-enabled devices was up 300% annually . 
Also of note will be any more details about the company’s recently announced restructuring plan. Pandora said in late January that it would eliminate some roles as it reoriented the company around “ad-tech and audience development efforts.” The company expects to save $45 million as a result of the restructuring and reinvest the savings “into growth initiatives including ad-tech, non-music content, device integration and marketing technology.”
Needham analyst Laura Martin flagged the company’s prediction that expenses would fall this year as a proportion of revenue and its interest in adding jobs in Atlanta, where costs are lower than Oakland, Calif., where Pandora is based. 
“Financially, for the first time in its history, Pandora’s management appears to be focused on bottom line momentum,” she wrote in a note to clients at the time. “Strategically, Pandora’s new CEO and CFO are focused on having Pandora do a few things best-in-class in order to maximize Pandora’s sale price to SiriusXM.”
Sirius XM Holdings Inc. SIRI, +0.00% was reportedly interested in acquiring Pandora last year, but a deal never emerged. Pandora settled for a strategic investment from Sirius instead, and that cash infusion is helping the streaming company fund some of its spending on business improvements.
Any updates on the relationship between the two companies would be interesting. Lynch told MarketWatch in January that he saw areas of potential collaboration as Pandora aims to move beyond just music and into other forms of audio.
